description: A fixed dataset plus a scoring rule, used to compare models on one capability.
Test questions or answers leaking into training data, so the model memorizes instead of solving and scores inflate.
When top models score near the ceiling, a benchmark stops separating them; small differences are noise or label errors.
A measure that becomes a target stops being a good measure. Explains leaderboard gaming without assuming bad faith.
A leaderboard built from human votes between two anonymous answers. Captures preference, including biases toward length, confidence and formatting.
Your own benchmark: real representative inputs, expected outcomes and scorers that match your product, run with your prompts while measuring cost and latency.
